title: Return actionable client errors for unknown models
description: TDD: replace transient 502 unknown-provider failures with deterministic 400 invalid_request_error responses that include a sorted, bounded list of currently routable models (including Sol, Luna, and Terra when registered), without auth details or blanket aliases. Cover Claude HTTP behavior and no-retry classification.
close_reason: Implemented TDD fix: unknown models return bounded dynamic catalog in 400 errors; Claude streaming and non-streaming integration covered

title: Fast cached replay across Claude and proxy restarts
description: Match Codex 0.144.5 restart semantics without persisting previous_response_id: after Claude/proxy restart, resume the same logical session, open a new WebSocket, perform one safe full replay with a deterministic prompt-cache scope and canonical stable prefix, observe cache reuse, then establish a fresh in-memory incremental response chain. Never reuse stale response IDs across process boundaries.
close_reason: Implemented end-to-end via TDD: deterministic cross-process cache identity, canonical request prefix, Codex-safe fresh response chains, privacy-safe observability/dashboard, true two-process E2E, and successful bounded live cache-hit probe.

title: Canonicalize cacheable Responses prefix across restarts
description: TDD: make equivalent Claude requests produce an identical cacheable Codex prefix across processes. Stabilize system/developer instructions, tool/schema ordering and serialization, compact summaries and replayed history. Keep request/run timestamps, trace metadata, random identifiers and transport-only fields outside the fingerprint. Changing model, instructions, tool schema or compact generation must change the prefix fingerprint.
close_reason: Cacheable Responses requests and fingerprints are canonical across JSON/tool ordering; RED/GREEN tests pass.

title: Enforce Codex-style safe restart replay semantics
description: Using Codex 0.144.5 as reference, TDD restart behavior: a fresh proxy process/new WebSocket must not restore or send a persisted previous_response_id. The first resumed turn sends full logical compacted history with the stable cache key; its successful response establishes a new in-memory chain; the next compatible turn is incremental. Invalidate on auth/model/prefix/compaction divergence and fall back safely on previous_response_not_found.
close_reason: Codex-style safe restart semantics verified: no stale response IDs across processes, fresh full replay then new incremental chain.

title: Add resume and cache effectiveness observability
description: Emit prompt-free metrics/traces for process-start generation, session resumed, new WebSocket, chain source (full_replay/incremental), chain reset reason, stable cache-scope result, prefix fingerprint continuity, replay body bytes, input/cache-read/output tokens, cache-read ratio and TTFT. Dashboards must compare first post-resume turn with subsequent incremental turns without recording payloads, raw cache keys, transcript text or high-cardinality session IDs.
close_reason: Chain source, reset reason, replay sizes, cache usage, traces/metrics, analyzer, docs, and Grafana panel added and tested.

title: Build two-process restart and resume E2E sandbox
description: Create a bounded sandbox test that starts proxy/Claude-compatible client process A for two turns, terminates both, starts fresh process B with the same session, and verifies: new socket; first resumed request has no previous_response_id; full compacted logical history; identical cache scope/prefix; new response ID; second turn incremental; model/auth/compaction changes invalidate safely. Preserve artifacts and fail with actionable diagnostics.
close_reason: True two-OS-process restart/resume E2E sandbox passes with stable cache key and isolated response chains.

title: Define deterministic cross-process prompt cache identity
description: TDD contract: derive prompt_cache_key/scope only from stable Claude logical session, auth/account boundary, provider and selected model family. Same inputs across fresh executor/process instances must produce the same key; session, account, provider or incompatible model changes must isolate it. Exclude run IDs, timestamps, ports, random UUIDs and telemetry metadata; never expose the raw private key in logs.
close_reason: Deterministic privacy-safe model/auth/session cache identity implemented and tested across store-independent calls.

title: Run bounded live cache-hit restart probe
description: After deterministic sandbox passes, run one low-cost live Sol probe: initial turn, clean proxy/Claude restart, resume same session, one resumed turn, one incremental turn. Capture run artifacts before cleanup and compare cached_tokens, cache-read ratio, TTFT, body bytes, connection source and chain source. Treat upstream cache reuse as TTL-dependent evidence, not a correctness requirement; cap turns/tokens and do not lose artifacts.
close_reason: Bounded live Sol resume probe passed: run 20260717T182730-8074a071 safely full-replayed without previous_response_id, matched scope/fingerprint from 20260717T182715-ec0685cb, and read 24064/25143 cached input tokens (95.7%).

title: Accelerate Claude Code over Codex WebSockets
description:
## Goal
Reduce proxy-induced latency for Claude Code root and subagent requests after speculative WebSocket preconnect landed.

## Scope
- Complete attributable observability.
- Remove same-session head-of-line blocking.
- Evaluate generate=false warmup.
- Improve repeated Luna prompt-cache reuse.
- Add bounded pool replenishment for bursts.

## Success Criteria
- Root and child latency can be decomposed from ingress through first upstream output.
- Optimizations preserve incremental/model-switching correctness and resource bounds.
- Race tests, full suite, and retained real Claude Code E2E artifacts validate the result.
close_reason: Completed attributable telemetry, same-session overflow, generate=false A/B, Luna prompt-cache reuse, and bounded burst replenishment. Full tests, race targets, builds, and retained real E2E evidence pass.

title: Evaluate Codex generate=false WebSocket warmup
description:
Hypothesis: after the WebSocket handshake, sending Codex-style response.create with generate=false may warm server-side routing and reduce time from child request_sent to first_upstream_event.

Implement as an opt-in experiment with TDD:
- Reproduce Codex 0.144.5 warmup semantics and completion handling without leaking a warmup response to downstream clients.
- Reuse the warmed socket for the real request and preserve model-switching correctness.
- Bound timeout, failures, 429 behavior, resource use, and fallback to pure preconnect.
- Emit warmup started/ready/failed timings and any returned response ID.

Acceptance:
- Synthetic protocol tests cover success, rejection, cancellation, and real-request reuse.
- Run repeated real A/B samples against pure handshake preconnect.
- Keep the feature only if median first_upstream_event improves materially without extra billed generation or instability; otherwise document and remove/leave disabled.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Synthetic tests cover success, rejection, cancellation, and real-request reuse.
2. Repeated real A/B samples compare against pure handshake preconnect.
3. No warmup response leaks downstream and no billed generation is introduced.
4. Keep enabled only if median first_upstream_event improves materially without instability.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Synthetic tests cover success, rejection, cancellation, and real-request reuse.
2. Repeated real A/B samples compare against pure handshake preconnect.
3. No warmup response leaks downstream and no billed generation is introduced.
4. Keep enabled only if median first_upstream_event improves materially without instability.
close_reason: Implemented opt-in Codex-style generate=false warmup with TDD, model-switching reuse, bounded failure handling, detached telemetry, and retained real A/B. Median request-to-first-event improved only 1.6% while child elapsed regressed 336ms, so feature remains disabled by default.

title: Add attributable Claude WebSocket latency telemetry
description:
Problem: current request logs prove speculative preconnect works, but reused=true conflates session reuse and pool leases, and cross-request root-to-child analysis requires manual timestamp reconstruction.

Implement with TDD:
- Add connection_source values for session_reuse, speculative, cold, retry, and overflow.
- Record session busy/queue time, in-flight preconnect wait, lease misses and miss reasons.
- Record bounded-pool state/counters: idle, dialing, expiry, discard, cooldown rejection.
- Emit normalized incremental reset reasons and usage/cache token metrics without prompt or credential contents.
- Add a stable privacy-safe root/agent correlation field across request artifacts.

Acceptance:
- Structured tests cover every new event and reserved-field protection.
- Existing request logs remain backward compatible.
- A synthetic root-to-Luna test produces a machine-readable phase timeline without parsing raw prompts.
- go test ./..., targeted race tests, and git diff --check pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Structured tests cover every new event and reserved-field protection.
2. Existing request logs remain backward compatible.
3. Synthetic root-to-Luna test emits a machine-readable prompt-free phase timeline.
4. Full suite, targeted race tests, and git diff --check pass.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Structured tests cover every new event and reserved-field protection.
2. Existing request logs remain backward compatible.
3. Synthetic root-to-Luna test emits a machine-readable prompt-free phase timeline.
4. Full suite, targeted race tests, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented privacy-safe correlation, connection-source attribution, lock contention, normalized usage/cache, incremental reset, and preconnect pool telemetry; targeted, race, full suite, and build pass.

title: Replenish bounded preconnect pool for Agent bursts
description:
Goal: keep later children warm when a root emits a small burst of Agent calls and earlier children consume the initial speculative sockets.

Implement with TDD:
- Replenish only after a successful lease or a newly observed unmatched Agent call.
- Respect the existing global cap, per-route auth isolation, TTL, in-flight accounting, auth generations, and 429 cooldown.
- Coalesce replenishment triggers and prevent reconnect loops after failures.
- Keep the feature independently configurable and disabled unless justified by burst E2E results.

Acceptance:
- Deterministic tests cover two/three parallel children, cap enforcement, failure cooldown, auth removal, expiry, and no duplicate dials.
- Race detector passes under concurrent lease/replenish/close.
- Real bounded burst E2E confirms connection_ready stays warm without exceeding the configured socket cap.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Tests cover parallel children, caps, cooldown, auth removal, expiry, and duplicate suppression.
2. Race detector passes concurrent lease/replenish/close.
3. Real bounded burst E2E keeps connection_ready warm without exceeding the configured cap.
4. Failure paths cannot create reconnect loops.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Tests cover parallel children, caps, cooldown, auth removal, expiry, and duplicate suppression.
2. Race detector passes concurrent lease/replenish/close.
3. Real bounded burst E2E keeps connection_ready warm without exceeding the configured cap.
4. Failure paths cannot create reconnect loops.
close_reason: Implemented opt-in lease replenishment with bounded atomic reservation, duplicate coalescing, cooldown/generation/TTL preservation, detached metrics, parallel/race tests, and retained real 3-child burst E2E; all children used speculative sockets within cap.

title: Measure and improve prompt-cache reuse for Luna agents
description:
Problem: the real Luna child probe reported cacheReadInputTokens=0 despite a root-scoped prompt-cache namespace. We need to distinguish expected first-use behavior from unstable prefixes or keys.

Implement with TDD and controlled E2E:
- Normalize cache read/write/input/output/reasoning usage into structured request metrics.
- Run two or more equivalent Luna children in the same root session and compare cache keys, stable system/tool prefixes, and usage.
- Identify mutations in tool definitions, instructions, identity headers, or request translation that defeat cache reuse.
- Improve only proxy-owned deterministic shaping; do not alter model effort or Claude semantics.

Acceptance:
- Tests prove cache key isolation across auth/model and sharing within the intended root/model scope.
- E2E artifacts retain both raw usage and normalized comparison.
- If cache hits are attainable, the second equivalent Luna request shows cache_read tokens and lower latency; otherwise document the upstream limitation with evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Tests prove cache-key isolation across auth/model and intended sharing within root/model scope.
2. E2E retains raw usage and normalized comparisons for repeated Luna children.
3. Proxy-owned shaping remains deterministic without changing effort or semantics.
4. Cache hits or the upstream limitation are demonstrated with retained evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Tests prove cache-key isolation across auth/model and intended sharing within root/model scope.
2. E2E retains raw usage and normalized comparisons for repeated Luna children.
3. Proxy-owned shaping remains deterministic without changing effort or semantics.
4. Cache hits or the upstream limitation are demonstrated with retained evidence.
close_reason: Added auth/model/root-isolated cache scopes, privacy-safe stable-prefix telemetry, and TDD. Retained real Luna E2E proves equivalent second child reads 4,864 of 5,113 input tokens from cache (95.1%); latency remained variable, so no latency claim.

title: Avoid same-session head-of-line blocking with overflow sockets
description:
Problem: real Claude Code E2E showed the primary request waiting about 2.89 seconds behind a concurrent title-generation request sharing one persistent session socket.

Implement with TDD:
- Detect a busy persistent session before blocking on its request lock.
- If the concurrent request cannot safely continue the active incremental chain, lease a speculative socket or use a one-shot overflow socket.
- Keep previous_response_id and incremental state owned exclusively by the canonical session request.
- Never multiplex two active responses on one upstream WebSocket.
- Preserve auth routing, cancellation, model switching, retry, and session capacity bounds.

Acceptance:
- A deterministic concurrent title-like plus main request test has no lock serialization and uses two sockets.
- Compatible sequential turns still reuse one socket and previous_response_id.
- Cancellation/error paths close overflow resources and do not corrupt canonical state.
- Stress and race tests pass.
- Real Claude Code A/B records session_lock wait and end-to-end improvement.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Concurrent incompatible requests use separate sockets without session-lock serialization.
2. Sequential compatible turns still reuse one socket and previous_response_id.
3. Cancellation and errors do not corrupt canonical incremental state.
4. Stress, race, full suite, and real Claude Code A/B pass.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Concurrent incompatible requests use separate sockets without session-lock serialization.
2. Sequential compatible turns still reuse one socket and previous_response_id.
3. Cancellation and errors do not corrupt canonical incremental state.
4. Stress, race, full suite, and real Claude Code A/B pass.
close_reason: Implemented non-blocking same-session overflow sockets with canonical incremental-state isolation and speculative lease support; 30x stress, race, full suite, build, and real Claude Code E2E passed.

title: TDD: safely recover Claude upstream WebSocket disconnects
close_reason: Implemented TDD-safe one-shot pre-output WebSocket retry, post-output SSE termination, retry OTEL metrics/traces, model-switch regression coverage, and fault-injection documentation.

title: Match Claude Code context-management expectations
description: Make the Anthropic compatibility facade and claudex-next launcher behave like Claude Code expects near context limits. Regression evidence: resumed root session ad953582 reached 200,687 input tokens, then the claude-api Skill injected an 808,206-byte tool_result; incremental and non-streaming requests failed with context-window overflow. Preserve request semantics unless an explicit context-management policy authorizes edits.

Cover custom model names, model switching, user overrides, invalid values, resume, and neutral launcher behavior. Document that /v1/models cannot communicate this reliably to Claude Code.

title: Implement accurate Anthropic count_tokens for routed GPT models
description: TDD: make POST /v1/messages/count_tokens estimate the translated target-model input, including system/messages/tool schemas/tool results/images/thinking and applicable context edits. Add golden parity tests against the Responses translation and model-switch cases; emit estimation method/error metrics. Never log payload content.

Return applied_edits and cleared counts in streaming and non-streaming Anthropic responses. Ensure tool_use/tool_result consistency, privacy, prompt-cache boundaries, and no implicit edits unless configured/requested.
close_reason: Implemented and regression-tested with Codex 0.144.5 context-window and error semantics as reference

title: Preflight Claude requests against effective context headroom
description: TDD: before upstream send, compute logical input plus reserved output against configured target-model context window for both full and incremental requests. Reject impossible requests immediately with Anthropic-compatible invalid_request_error/Prompt is too long; distinguish input overflow from raw-body limits. Do not retry or change transport for deterministic overflow.
close_reason: Implemented and regression-tested with Codex 0.144.5 context-window and error semantics as reference

title: Normalize context-overflow streaming and fallback semantics
description: TDD regression for an upstream SSE type:error context overflow received inside HTTP 200. Classify it as terminal context_overflow before meaningful output, preserve exact Anthropic error semantics, avoid transport-failure classification and useless proxy retries, and make streaming/non-streaming behavior consistent. Verify Claude Code recognizes the response shape.

title: Observe context pressure and giant tool results without payload leakage

Never export tool names, arguments, result bodies, prompts, session IDs, or raw errors. Add Grafana panels and runbook queries.

title: Preserve safe previous_response_id chains across reconnects

Reuse only for the same auth/account, model, logical Claude session, and uncompacted history; invalidate on model switch, compaction boundary, auth change, divergence, or upstream rejection. Preflight controlled full replay and expose why a chain was reused or discarded.
